Use the toolbar to change style and color without leaving a category. Appearance on the first screen provides 150% text and a 360 dp viewport. Use Android settings for real font/display scaling, rotation and TalkBack. Demo controls never change device settings.
A very long title for an application or setting that must wrap without hiding the controls

Long descriptions remain readable when text grows or the screen becomes narrow. Content determines the row height; neither the title nor the supporting information is truncated. Check scrolling and touch targets as well as visual alignment.
Tap the entire row. No application navigation is performed in this example.
The setting and its effective status are separate values.
This row announces status changes and has no click action.
The caller owns the operation. While loading, the action is disabled to prevent duplicate requests.
Supporting slot: release notes, help or host-owned links can go here.
The choice dialog edits a draft. Cancel, Back or outside dismissal leaves the committed value unchanged. Confirmation uses the official AlertDialog directly.
This is a preview of a guarded change. Read the explanation and confirm deliberately. Cancellation never changes the setting. No device configuration or saved application data is modified.
Inspired by shared patterns in ShutUp, Glyph Barty and Scheduler. This screen uses Pyrite defaults and simulated state; it contains no app logic or assets.
Turning on requires confirmation. Turning off applies immediately.
Explore Pyrite standard UI by category. Use the toolbar to change design and color.
